nodes.label: The three-body solution derived from The Method 1.6
nodes.rationale: Every component of the Gemini paper is an instance of a construct the book already proves, and the book states in advance both what the solution must look like and what it cannot contain: the paper is Chapter 31 run to completion on three bodies.

nodes.label: Master Theorem stratification as a complete index with E = 0
nodes.rationale: Five measure-disjoint exhaustive cells means E = 0, and by §25.6 a complete index predicts no individual cell — which is why §5 must add the Kolmogorov clause. 'Completely solvable' and 'envelope precision only' are one statement, and Poincare is untouched by both.

nodes.label: Three excluded constraint forms carried at once
nodes.rationale: The Gemini potential shows a sum (superposed pairwise terms), a difference (Jacobi vectors) and a symmetric function (the degree-8 variety in power sums) — the maximal case of what Chapter 18 forbids — so its exact region is not a lattice and the strata can only be a monotone envelope.

nodes.label: Shape-sphere quotient as the certificate of closure
nodes.rationale: Quotienting 18 dimensions by translations, rotations and scale is 'drop a coordinate' in §18.4.1's sense four times over, and Montgomery's S^2 is the fixed point that exhibits closure — the realiser of §18.4.1 applied to three bodies.

nodes.label: Maupertuis time elimination — cells that are not moves
nodes.rationale: An index has a time column exactly when its cells are moves; shape-space cells are positions, so the column is removable and the geodesic equations with rational Christoffel symbols are the path-independent physics. Time returns afterwards as a quadrature, which is where the transcendental part sits.

nodes.label: The one-level consistency deficit and the bracket
nodes.rationale: R is pairwise, K3 needs strong 3-consistency, and the shortfall is exactly one level; the book's single genuinely ternary object is the bracket T(n-1), T(n), T(n+1) with no pair determining the third. The three-body problem is celestial mechanics' ternary object, so its solution can only be a bracket.

nodes.label: Audit flags not yet run (D2 check, Saari, attribution)
nodes.rationale: Gemini's coefficients and the degree-8 polynomial are stated rather than derived so a second route is owed; the measure-disjointness needs the collision set to be measure zero with Saari's status cited; and the attribution table omits Moeckel and Chenciner-Montgomery for the figure-eight braid.
